reading: Grey pieces at the bottom are jigsaw pieces; each slides (up and sideways) into the hole of the red ceiling whose shape it fills, and is recoloured blue; the grey originals vanish.

slots.holes: background notches in the red top band (plus the open row below it)
slots.match: each piece goes to the hole its shape exactly fills (translation only)
slots.colour: placed piece becomes 1; source cells become 0

why: blue cells in the output are exactly the grey pieces translated so their top part fills each red-band hole

reading: Output is the red square outline cut out; the small 3x3 pattern elsewhere is scaled up by (frame interior size / 3) to fill the frame interior.

slots.frame: the red rectangular outline (output = its box)

why: output box = red outline box; interior = pattern upscaled by integer factor

reading: Every 3x3 hollow blue square (ring around one background cell) is replaced in place by a red plus sign; other shapes stay.

new_rows.name: ring_hole
new_rows.datalog:
nb(Y, X, count(DY, DX)) :- px(Y, X, 0), off(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, C).
ring_hole(Y, X) :- nb(Y, X, N), N = 8.

why: each background cell with all 8 neighbours coloured gets the 3x3 unit 020/222/020 centred on it (its 0 corners overwrite the ring corners)

reading: Objects of 4 or more cells fall straight down until they touch the bottom border; smaller objects (single cells, short lines, 3-cell L) stay put.

new_rows.name: big
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
big(Y, X) :- obj(O, Y, X), osize(O, N), N > 3.

why: each object with >3 cells is translated down so its lowest row is the last grid row, shape unchanged

reading: In the noisy grid, each 3x3 square made entirely of 0 is filled with 1 (scanning top-left first, a square overlapping an already chosen one is skipped).

new_rows.name: zero_square
new_rows.datalog:
z(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, 0).
nz(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !z(Y, X).
dirty(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C0), nz(A, B), Y3 = Y + 2, X3 = X + 2, A >= Y, A <= Y3, B >= X, B <= X3.
sq(Y, X) :- z(Y, X), Y3 = Y + 2, X3 = X + 2, px(Y3, X3, C), !dirty(Y, X).
ov(Y, X) :- sq(Y, X), sq(A, B), Ylo = Y - 3, Xlo = X - 3, Xhi = X + 3, A < Y, A > Ylo, B > Xlo, B < Xhi.
ov(Y, X) :- sq(Y, X), sq(A, B), Xlo = X - 3, A = Y, B < X, B > Xlo.
keep(Y, X) :- sq(Y, X), !ov(Y, X).
zero_square(A, B) :- keep(Y, X), px(A, B, C), Y3 = Y + 2, X3 = X + 2, A >= Y, A <= Y3, B >= X, B <= X3.

why: exactly the cells of non-overlapping all-0 3x3 squares become 1

reading: The grid is 3x3 panels split by grey lines; the panel containing a yellow 4 is copied into the panel whose position matches the 4's position inside its panel; all other panels are cleared to 0.

slots.panels: 9 panels cut by the grey separators
slots.destination: panel index = (row, col) of the 4 within its 3x3 panel
slots.rest: all other panels emptied; separators kept

why: output = separators + source panel content at destination panel, zeros elsewhere

reading: A hat-shaped object shelters the columns below it; in each hat column that contains a marker dot below the hat, a vertical line of the marker colour is drawn from just under the hat down to the bottom border.

slots.triggers: markers below the hat within its column span
slots.line: from the cell under the hat's lowest cell in that column to the bottom border

why: new cells are exactly the vertical runs below the hat in columns holding a marker beneath it
invariants: markers outside hat columns get no line

reading: Output is a 3x3 grey line chosen by the number of distinct colours in the input: 1 colour -> top row, 2 colours -> main diagonal, 3 colours -> anti-diagonal; rest 0.

slots.count: number of distinct colours in input

why: the grey line chosen by the distinct-colour count

reading: Each 3-cell L (2x2 box missing one corner) shoots a diagonal ray of its colour out of its missing corner, starting one step beyond that corner and running to the grid border.

slots.direction: diagonal from the L's elbow cell through its missing corner
slots.start: cell diagonally beyond the missing corner

why: new cells are exactly the diagonal rays beyond each L's missing corner

reading: The output doubles the width: the input plus its left-right mirror image with colours inverted (0->8, 2->0), the mirror attached on the side where the red shape touches the edge so the reds meet in the middle.

slots.side: copy placed on the side of the input edge column that contains red (left in pair 1,2; right in 0,3)

why: output = [input | inverted mirror] or [inverted mirror | input]
invariants: original input appears unchanged in one half
